methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $690M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Bethlehem Steel Corp is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $690M to date. The valuation exercise references a comparable universe of nine peers in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, comprising one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity.

Given the absence of sufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage peers meeting minimum sample thresholds, the Peer-Median method is not applicable. The Stage-Progression method is the only tractable approach, applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier to the $690M raised proxy to account for typical Growth-to-next-stage value progression. This yields an implied valuation of $828M.

The triangulated valuation range spans $704M (low) to $952M (high), with a median of $828M. This single-method analysis carries material uncertainty given reliance on a standardized step-up multiple in the absence of direct comparable transaction or trading data. Key unknowns include company-specific margin trajectory, customer concentration, and technology differentiation relative to the broader peer set. The wide $248M interquartile spread reflects the inherent imprecision of stage-based extrapolation without anchoring peer multiples.
